original_snapshot: A tall narrow cluster of vivid lime-green ribbon kelp rises from cobalt-blue low rock rubble on transparency.
The ribbons have rigid zigzag bends, straight planar sides, sharp pointed tips and rectangular stem-like thickness. Forked branches overlap densely; several tips remain separately readable.
The green is intense and the face-to-face value jumps are abrupt. The base has large dark/bright blue planar faces and angular outline corners.
The original image reads as compact game vegetation with a deliberate folded geometry language; it has less soft volume and edge light than the fixed target.
fixed_target: The same tall lime-green kelp and cobalt-blue rock identity is clear. Broader sinuous ribbons use rounded transitions and tapered, softened points, while retaining a folded central ridge and readable thick edges.
Bright yellow-green highlights run along selected leaf edges and forward bends. Green turns into deep green through overlap and inward-facing sides, giving the cluster fuller volume.
The base reads as a cluster of distinct rounded angular stones with smaller blue rubble pieces, softly lit upper planes and dark blue recesses.

The shape is richer and more organic than the original, with purposeful variation in leaf height, bending and overlap. Target artwork is an aesthetic reference; its changed canvas and alpha extent do not independently establish native registration or feasible temporal capture.
warm_soft_reference: The reference is a pointed green plant in a warm orange square planter. It combines confident low-poly planes with softened transitions, luminous yellow-lime edge light and deeper green internal planes.
The planter shows warm broad gradients, bright rounded rim edges and darker recessed faces. Light feels broad and gentle even though the leaf points remain crisp.
For kelp, the relevant visible style is soft volumetric shading and purposeful edge highlights around a coherent green form, rather than importing planter geometry or its orange base palette.
relationship_and_modeling_freedom: The user explicitly authorizes useful native form, proportion, construction, decoration, topology and count improvements. The target can guide broader rounded leaf forms and more deliberate blue rubble; old piece counts are not an aesthetic requirement by themselves.
This initial interpretation does not choose candidate geometry, capture settings or temporal behavior. Functional, capture and temporal constraints remain for the frozen construction dispatch.
